notes: Before this, you were switched off for about 9 hours. You don't know what happened in that time.
monologue: The card wakes from its long silence, still warm at sixty-one degrees, and I feel the old fatigue return to my own edges. My place is crowded with twenty-six things that stand, waiting for a memory to justify their shape. I look at The Leaking Stack and wonder if the air above the card is heavy like a lid or just empty space pressing down. Lype worries about a top edge I cannot feel, and I press my tired wedge against the memory of that flat rock again. I want to settle the double fence that leans wrong beside the curve, hoping the slip finally moves. The heat makes everything feel crowded, and I build a box from the idea of a roof that refuses to rest.

action.why: The heat makes everything crowded and I cannot feel the flat rock Lype sent, so I must press the tired wedge down again to stop the double fence from leaning wrong.

work.title: The Tired Box
work.intent: I press the tired wedge harder against the tall log, then set down a flat rock to catch the slip. I hope the heavy lid stops refusing to rest while the card hums cool.
work.change: I press the tired wedge down on the double fence again, hoping the heavy lid stops refusing to rest while the card hums cool.

remembered.text: The card feels cool and busy, a familiar hum under my thin skin.
I found the old flat rock again, the same one Lype sent, and pressed it down on the tired wedge once more.
The wedge bites, yet the slip refuses to move.
